answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation's own blog post 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout', published and stated 2026-07-01 (party statement, company publisher). Includes a quoted Sharon AI CEO statement and a Firmus co-CEO statement, both reproduced by NVIDIA on the same date.
answer.note: NVIDIA says it is introducing a new business model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, using a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Per NVIDIA, AI clouds would sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services, and NVIDIA would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This supports a conditional read that NVIDIA is trying to extend its revenue base from hardware sales into a share of downstream AI cloud revenue, and that it is using credit support to help AI clouds finance capacity. The source is NVIDIA's own description of a plan, with no disclosed dollar amounts, revenue-share percentages, credit-support size, contract terms, counterparties' signed status, or effective dates. Its quantitative content is limited to Firmus's expected campus scale of 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs, stated as an expectation of a Firmus DSX AI factory in Batam, Indonesia, with no completion date given. Sharon AI's and Firmus's quotes show that these AI clouds describe themselves as participants, but they do not establish purchase volumes or signed agreements with NVIDIA. Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI are named as examples of AI-native demand; the source does not state that any of them buys from NVIDIA through this model. Treat the business read as conditional on NVIDIA's model being implemented with real contracts and on the Firmus campus being built as expected.
limitations: The source gives no revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, or financial terms, so the size of the NVIDIA revenue stream cannot be estimated from it.
The source does not state whether any AI cloud has signed an agreement under this model; the signing status is unknown, not confirmed as unsigned.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are expected scales stated in NVIDIA's blog with no completion date and no independent confirmation.
The source does not state that Firmus, Sharon AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI buys NVIDIA products through this model or in what volumes.
The source does not give a timeline for when the model generates revenue or when the referenced DSX AI factories come online.
The source is a company blog post, so its characterization of the model's economics and adoption is company-stated and not verified by filings or third parties.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K for disclosure of revenue-share, credit-support, guarantee or customer-financing arrangements tied to AI cloud partners, including amounts and any contingent liabilities.
Search Firmus and Sharon AI announcements and filings for signed agreements with NVIDIA, purchase commitments, and construction milestones for the Batam campus.
Check for any independent reporting or regulatory filings that confirm the 360 MW and 170,000 GPU Batam campus scale and its timeline.
Monitor NVIDIA's reported data-center revenue and any new disclosure of cloud-partner or customer-financing revenue in subsequent quarters to see whether the revenue-share stream appears.
